## Data

```{r}
master_nys <- read_csv("../../data/final/master_nys.csv")
#master_nys <- read_csv("data/final/master_nys.csv")
```

```{r}
hist(master_nys$dv_female_rate)
```

Derived variables used across the models below: log-transformed population and
income (both highly skewed, so log is the appropriate scale for a linear
model), a non-white population share, and sex-offense domestic violence rates
broken out by female and male victims specifically.

```{r}
master_nys <- master_nys %>%
  mutate(
    log_pop = log(tot_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc),
    pct_nonwhite = 1 - pct_white,
    dv_sex_offense_female_rate = `Sex Offense_female_intimate_partner` / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_sex_offense_male_rate   = `Sex Offense_male_intimate_partner` / tot_pop * 100000,
    num_prisons = factor(num_prisons)
  ) %>% 
  
```

```{r}
nyc_geoids <- c("36005", "36047", "36061", "36081", "36085")  # Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens, Richmond
  
nys_no_nyc <- master_nys %>% 
  filter(!GEOID %in% nyc_geoids)
  
nys_no_nyc_2224 <- master_nys %>%
  filter(year >= 2022, !GEOID %in% nyc_geoids)
```

---

## Variable Definitions

**Exposure variables** (the prison-presence measures being studied):

- `prison_present` — binary indicator, any open prison in the county
- `num_open` — count of open prisons in the county

**Outcome variables** (what the exposure is hypothesized to affect):

- Domestic violence: `dv_total_rate`, `dv_female_rate`, `dv_male_rate`, `dv_agg_assault_rate`, `dv_sex_offense_rate`, `dv_sex_offense_female_rate`, `dv_sex_offense_male_rate`
- Mortality/distress: `overdose_rate`, `suicide_rate`, `homicide_rate`
- Household/economic: `divorce_rate`, `life_exp_weighted`, `medhhinc`

**Confounders** (pre-existing county characteristics that could affect both
prison siting and the outcomes above — these belong in the model as controls):

- `pct_nonwhite`, `log_medhhinc`, `poverty_rate`, `unemp_rate`, `RUCC_2023`, `pct_bachelors_plus`, `log_pop`
- `single_parent_rate` is a judgment call: plausibly a pre-existing confounder, but worth flagging as a limitation rather than treating as clean-cut

**Mediators** (variables that sit *between* exposure and outcome — plausible
consequences of prison presence rather than pre-existing causes of it). These
are deliberately **excluded** from the main models, since controlling for a
mediator blocks the causal pathway being estimated; they are examined
separately as robustness/mechanism checks instead:

- `correctional_emplvl_rate` — prisons bring correctional jobs, which may affect household dynamics
- `n_deaths`, `n_suicides` (in-custody) — consequences of having a prison, not pre-existing county traits
- `staffing_gap_pct` — also downstream of prison presence

---

## Analysis: Prison Presence (Binary)

Exploratory comparison of county-year outcomes by whether the county has an
open prison. **Caveat:** this is a county-*year* panel (each county appears up
to 6 times), so a plain two-sample t-test treats repeated observations from
the same county as independent, which they are not — p-values here should be
read as a first look, not a final result. The clustered-SE models further
below are the more defensible version for anything reported formally.

```{r}
table(master_nys$prison_present)
```

```{r}
vars_to_test <- c(
  dv_total_rate = "DV Rate (Total)",
  dv_female_rate = "DV Rate (Female victims)",
  dv_male_rate = "DV Rate (Male victims)",
  dv_agg_assault_rate = "DV Rate (Agg. Assault)",
  dv_sex_offense_rate = "DV Rate (Sex Offense)",
  suicide_rate = "Suicide Rate (community)",
  overdose_rate = "Overdose Rate",
  homicide_rate = "Homicide Rate",
  life_exp_weighted = "Life Expectancy",
  divorce_rate = "Divorce Rate",
  medhhinc = "Median HH Income",
  poverty_rate = "Poverty Rate",
  unemp_rate = "Unemployment Rate",
  homeown_rate = "Homeownership Rate",
  pct_bachelors_plus = "% Bachelor's+",
  single_parent_rate = "Single-Parent Rate"
)

run_ttest_table <- function(data, title, subtitle) {
  results <- lapply(names(vars_to_test), function(v) {
    d <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
    t_result <- t.test(d[[v]] ~ d$prison_present)
    tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]],
      mean_no_prison = t_result$estimate[1],
      mean_prison = t_result$estimate[2],
      difference = t_result$estimate[2] - t_result$estimate[1],
      p_value = t_result$p.value
    )
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  results %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      variable = "Variable", mean_no_prison = "No Prison",
      mean_prison = "Prison Present", difference = "Difference", p_value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference), decimals = 3) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05))
}

run_ttest_table(
  master_nys,
  "NY County Outcomes by Prison Presence",
  "Two-sample t-tests, county-year observations, 2019-2024"
)
```

### Year-by-year comparison

Splitting the pooled panel by year shows whether the pattern is consistent
across time or driven by a specific year. **Caveat:** each single-year table
uses only ~62 NY counties split between groups, so estimates here are noisier
and p-values more volatile than the pooled version above — treat any one
year's "significant" result with extra caution rather than as a standalone
finding.

```{r}
years_available <- sort(unique(master_nys$year))
years_available
```

```{r}
run_ttest_table(
  master_nys %>% filter(year == years_available[1]),
  paste("NY County Outcomes by Prison Presence —", years_available[1]),

)

```

## Analysis: Prison Presence, County-Clustered Standard Errors

The plain t-tests above treat each county-year row as independent, which
overstates statistical confidence given the panel structure. These models
correct for that by clustering standard errors at the county level, with and
without year fixed effects (which absorb any NY-wide shock in a given year,
e.g. COVID-era disruptions, common to all counties).

```{r}
clustered_results <- lapply(names(vars_to_test), function(v) {
  d <- master_nys %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))

  if (n_distinct(d$prison_present) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]], mean_no_prison = NA_real_,
      estimate = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }

  model <- feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ prison_present")), data = d, cluster = ~GEOID)
  tidy_model <- tidy(model)
  intercept_row <- tidy_model %>% filter(term == "(Intercept)")
  prison_row <- tidy_model %>% filter(term == "prison_present")

  if (nrow(intercept_row) == 0 | nrow(prison_row) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]], mean_no_prison = NA_real_,
      estimate = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }

  tibble(
    variable = vars_to_test[[v]],
    mean_no_prison = intercept_row$estimate,
    estimate = prison_row$estimate,
    std_error = prison_row$std.error,
    p_value = prison_row$p.value,
    n = nrow(d)
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

clustered_results %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable", mean_no_prison = "No Prison (baseline)",
    estimate = "Effect of Prison Presence", std_error = "SE", p_value = "p-value", n = "N"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, estimate, std_error), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Effect of Prison Presence on County Outcomes",
    subtitle = "OLS with county-clustered standard errors, 2019-2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value >= 0.05 & p_value < 0.10))
```

```{r}
clustered_results_fe <- lapply(names(vars_to_test), function(v) {
  d <- master_nys %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))

  if (n_distinct(d$prison_present) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]], estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }

  model <- feols(as.formula(paste(v, "~ prison_present | year")), data = d, cluster = ~GEOID)
  tidy_model <- tidy(model)
  prison_row <- tidy_model %>% filter(term == "prison_present")

  if (nrow(prison_row) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]], estimate = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d)
    ))
  }

  tibble(
    variable = vars_to_test[[v]],
    estimate = prison_row$estimate,
    std_error = prison_row$std.error,
    p_value = prison_row$p.value,
    n = nrow(d)
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

clustered_results_fe %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable", estimate = "Effect of Prison Presence",
    std_error = "SE", p_value = "p-value", n = "N"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std_error), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Effect of Prison Presence on County Outcomes",
    subtitle = "OLS with year fixed effects, county-clustered SEs, 2019-2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value >= 0.05 & p_value < 0.10))
```

## Analysis: Number of Open Prisons (Continuous)

Rather than a binary presence indicator, these models use `num_open` (count of
open prisons in the county) as the variable of interest, with a full set of
county-level confounder controls. Each table shows the full model, not just
the coefficient of interest, so the behavior of controls can be checked
alongside it.

```{r}
controls <- "pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop"

term_labels <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  "num_open" = "Number of Open Prisons",
  "pct_nonwhite" = "% Non-White",
  "log_medhhinc" = "Log(Median HH Income)",
  "poverty_rate" = "Poverty Rate",
  "unemp_rate" = "Unemployment Rate",
  "RUCC_2023" = "Rurality (RUCC)",
  "pct_bachelors_plus" = "% Bachelor's+",
  "log_pop" = "Log(Population)"
)

run_full_model_table <- function(v, label, data, controls) {
  # Avoid regressing income on itself when income is both outcome and control
  ctrl_set <- if (v == "medhhinc") gsub(" \\+ log_medhhinc", "", controls) else controls
  d <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(num_open))

  formula_str <- paste(v, "~ num_open +", ctrl_set)
  model <- feols(as.formula(formula_str), data = d, cluster = ~GEOID)

  tidy(model) %>%
    mutate(term_label = ifelse(term %in% names(term_labels), term_labels[term], term)) %>%
    select(term_label, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      term_label = "Term", estimate = "Estimate", std.error = "SE",
      statistic = "t value", p.value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, statistic), decimals = 3) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
    tab_header(
      title = paste("Outcome:", label),
      subtitle = paste0("OLS, county-clustered SEs, N = ", nobs(model))
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value >= 0.05 & p.value < 0.10))
}
```

```{r}
run_full_model_table("overdose_rate", "Overdose Rate", master_nys, controls)
```

### Collinearity check

```{r}
master_nys %>%
  select(unemp_rate, poverty_rate, log_medhhinc, RUCC_2023) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")
```

```{r}
model_vif <- lm(dv_female_rate ~ num_open + pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop, data = master_nys)
vif(model_vif)
```

VIFs are all well under the conventional 5–10 concern threshold, so
multicollinearity does not explain the unemployment coefficient's direction.

### Outlier / influence check

```{r}
d <- master_nys %>% filter(!is.na(dv_female_rate), !is.na(unemp_rate))
d %>% arrange(desc(unemp_rate)) %>% select(county_name, year, unemp_rate, dv_female_rate) %>% head(10)
d %>% arrange(unemp_rate) %>% select(county_name, year, unemp_rate, dv_female_rate) %>% head(10)
```

The negative unemployment–DV relationship holds across multiple counties and
years (e.g. Sullivan, Broome at the high-unemployment end), not just a single
outlier row.

### Robustness to adding single-parent rate

```{r}
model_robust <- feols(dv_female_rate ~ num_open + pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop + single_parent_rate, data = master_nys, cluster = ~GEOID)
summary(model_robust)
```


### DV data reporting consistency

Administrative domestic violence data is known to undercount actual incidence
and to do so unevenly across jurisdictions; this checks at least whether all
counties report consistently across all years (a coarse, necessary but not
sufficient check — it cannot detect *within-report* underreporting).

```{r}
master_nys %>%
  group_by(county_name) %>%
  summarise(n_years_reported = sum(!is.na(dv_female_rate))) %>%
  arrange(n_years_reported)
```

All non-NYC counties report in all 6 years; NYC boroughs report 0 (excluded
from this DCJS file at the source, consistent with the "NON-NEW YORK CITY
COUNTIES" filtering applied during data cleaning). Reporting-volume gaps are
therefore ruled out, though differences in underlying reporting *rate* across
counties remain an unresolvable limitation of administrative DV data.

## Analysis: Specification Curve (Independent Confounder Blocks)

Each table below adds `num_open` plus *one* confounder block on its own
(demographics, economic, rurality, education), rather than building
cumulatively — the "No Controls" and "+ Full" specifications serve as the two
anchor points, and each middle table shows how a single block shifts the
estimate and standard error in isolation from the others.

```{r}
specs <- list(
  "No Controls" = "num_open",
  "+ Demographics" = "num_open + pct_nonwhite",
  "+ Economic" = "num_open + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate",
  "+ Rurality" = "num_open + RUCC_2023",
  "+ Education" = "num_open + pct_bachelors_plus",
  "+ Full" = "num_open + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop"
)

run_spec_table <- function(outcome, spec_name, data) {
  d <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]]), !is.na(num_open))
  formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", specs[[spec_name]])
  model <- feols(as.formula(formula_str), data = d, cluster = ~GEOID)

  tidy(model) %>%
    mutate(term_label = ifelse(term %in% names(term_labels), term_labels[term], term)) %>%
    select(term_label, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      term_label = "Term", estimate = "Estimate", std.error = "SE",
      statistic = "t value", p.value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, statistic), decimals = 3) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
    tab_header(
      title = paste0("Outcome: ", outcome, " — ", spec_name),
      subtitle = paste0("OLS, county-clustered SEs, N = ", nobs(model))
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value >= 0.05 & p.value < 0.10))
}
```
